text: The wreck is at ninety metres and the weather turns Thursday. Are you taking the job or not?
We're taking it.
We are not taking it. The compressor has been rebuilt twice this year.
Then we rebuild it a third time. Nobody goes in the water until it holds pressure for an hour. You have my word on that.
Hand me the manifold wrench and stop looking at the clock.
Forty minutes of pressure and it's already dropping.
Then it does not hold. That is what dropping means.
Suit up. We dive at first light.
You said an hour. It did not make forty minutes.
I said a lot of things. The weather turns Thursday.
That is the second time this year you have told me a rule and then moved it.
If you go down on that compressor and something happens, the insurance does not pay and I do not cover you.
Nothing is going to happen.
That is not a plan. That is a mood.
My sister's wedding is on the sixteenth. I told her I would be there.
Then you will be there. I will take your rotation myself if it comes to that.
You do not have to do that.
I know. I am doing it anyway.
Sixty metres. The hull is intact and the cargo hold is dry.
Pressure is unstable. Vale, come up.
Ten more minutes.
Now, Vale.
The claim came back denied. I warned you it would.
I will make it right. Every peso, out of my share, before the season ends.
Say that again in writing and I might believe it.
He tells you what you want and then does what he wanted.
He is not lying when he says it. That is the part that makes it hard.
You said you would sign my dive log so I could sit the certification.
I will. Tonight.
You said tonight three nights ago.
Give me the log. I will sign it as supervising diver and Vale can argue with the board if he likes.
The harbour master wants the mooring cleared by Friday. You told him Wednesday.
Then he gets it Wednesday.
With what crew? Marisol is ashore and Teddy is at a wedding.
I am going ashore for a week. Do not call me unless the boat is sinking.
I will not call.
It has been eleven hours.
The boat is almost sinking. That is close enough.
